name: SN1
steps: 2 steps (slow ionization to carbocation, fast nucleophilic capture)
intermediate: Carbocation (sp² hybridized, planar with empty p orbital)
stereochemistry: Racemization with slight excess of inversion due to ion-pair shielding
rearrangements: Common (1,2-hydride and 1,2-methyl shifts to more stable cations)
substrate: 3° >> 2° (1° and methyl do not react without resonance stabilization)
nucleophile: Weak, neutral nucleophiles acceptable (H₂O, MeOH, EtOH); concentration does not affect rate
solvent: Polar protic (H₂O, MeOH, EtOH) to stabilize ions and lower activation energy
temperature: Low to moderate temperature (high temperature promotes competing E1)
energyProfile: Two transition states (TS1 rate-limiting) and one carbocation intermediate trough
summary: A two-step substitution mechanism in which heterolytic C-LG cleavage forms a planar carbocation, which is subsequently captured by a nucleophile from either face.

name: SN2
steps: 1 step (concerted backside attack simultaneously displacing leaving group)
intermediate: None (single pentacoordinate trigonal bipyramidal transition state)
substrate: CH₃ > 1° > 2° >> 3° (tertiary is unreactive due to steric hindrance; neopentyl is extremely slow)
nucleophile: Strong, polarizable nucleophiles required (I⁻, CN⁻, RS⁻, N₃⁻, OH⁻, RO⁻)
solvent: Polar aprotic (DMSO, DMF, acetone, MeCN) to leave nucleophilic anions unshielded
temperature: Low to moderate temperature (high temperature promotes competing E2)
energyProfile: Single smooth activation energy hill with one transition state and no intermediates
summary: A concerted bimolecular substitution occurring via collinear 180° backside attack with complete Walden inversion of configuration.

name: E1
steps: 2 steps (slow ionization to carbocation, fast β-proton abstraction)
stereochemistry: Non-stereospecific (gives E/Z mixtures; more stable E-isomer predominates)
regiochemistry: Zaitsev's rule (more substituted, more stable alkene is major product)
rearrangements: Common (1,2-hydride and 1,2-methyl shifts to more stable cations)
substrate: 3° >> 2° (1° and methyl do not react without resonance stabilization)
nucleophile: Weak base (solvent like H₂O, EtOH); base concentration does not affect rate
solvent: Polar protic (H₂O, EtOH, MeOH) to solvate departing ions
temperature: High temperature (heat / reflux) strongly favors E1 over SN1 due to favorable entropy (ΔS° > 0)
energyProfile: Two transition states (TS1 ionization rate-limiting) with carbocation intermediate well
summary: A two-step elimination sharing the carbocation intermediate with SN1. Deprotonation of a β-hydrogen by a weak base yields the more stable Zaitsev alkene.

name: E2
steps: 1 step (concerted β-deprotonation, π-bond formation, and leaving group departure)
stereochemistry: Anti-periplanar requirement (180° dihedral angle; trans-diaxial in cyclohexanes)
regiochemistry: Zaitsev product with small base (OH⁻, EtO⁻); Hofmann product with bulky base (KOtBu, DBU, LDA)
substrate: 3° > 2° > 1° (steric bulk on substrate favors E2 over SN2)
nucleophile: Strong base required (NaOH, NaOEt, KOtBu, DBU, LDA)
solvent: Polar aprotic or polar protic (with high concentration of strong base)
temperature: High temperature strongly favors E2 over SN2 due to favorable entropy
energyProfile: Single concerted transition state requiring simultaneous C-H and C-LG bond changes
summary: A concerted single-step elimination requiring an anti-periplanar 180° alignment of β-H and leaving group. A strong base abstracts the proton as the π bond forms.
